title: Holistic model scouting demo: heuristics to bench
summary: Intro demo of Redwood model catalog + Optimize tooling focused on how we pick open models, run quick benches, and map compatibility matrixes for production constraints. Went through heuristic shortlist, live bench plan, routing variants and tradeoffs (latency vs cost, hosted vs dedicated), security requirements. Agreed next steps: send tailored bench script, security pack, and schedule pilot kick-off call.
action_items: Priya Nair: share bench script + sample prompt set by 2027-09-17
Ravi Patel: provide dataset size and compliance constraints (data residency) by 2027-09-20
Ethan Brooks: prepare initial Dedicated capacity estimate and rough cost delta by 2027-09-20
next_steps: Redwood to send model-scouting deck + bench script link
Schedule 60m pilot kickoff (include infra + security) week of 2027-09-27
Run 48-hour shortlist bench on Redwood hosted region us-east-1
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-14 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Brooks (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Product); Ravi Patel (VesperData CTO), Laura Kim (ML Platform), Jonas Meyer (Infra), Sofia Alvarez (PM)
Links shared: https://redwood.ai/decks/model-scout-deck.pdf , https://redwood.ai/bench-scripts/scout-v1.zip

Agenda: quick intros, walkthrough model catalog scouting flow, live bench plan, compatibility matrix and routing, Q&A, next steps

[00:00] Maya Chen: ok hi everyone, thanks for joining, uh, we're gonna show a quick end-to-end of how a team at Redwood would go from open-model shortlist to a bench and then to a compatibility matrix and routing plan. Ethan will lead the bench bits. Priya is on product to show the picklist heuristics.

[00:22] Ravi Patel: Hey thanks, quick note, timeline is tight for us — we want something in prod-ish in 8 weeks if possible. Also we have strict EU data residency for some features.

[00:40] Ethan Brooks: Great, thanks Ravi. We'll keep residency in mind — we'll show both hosted and dedicated options and how the catalog flags model variants that have on-prem or region-ready builds. Small note: the console sometimes displays "Redwood Catalogue" in the transcript, that's just the UI label.

[01:05] Laura Kim: Can you also confirm what metrics you surface during bench? We care about p95 latency for short chat interactions and cost per 1k tokens for long form.

[01:22] Ethan Brooks: Yep, p50/p95/token cost/throughput/kv-cache-hit-rate. In the bench plan we instrument the runtime to capture kernel-level fallbacks — like when FP16 kernels hit limits we opt for quantized kernels, that'll show up in the compat matrix.

[02:01] Priya Nair: I'll jump into the catalog heuristics. Our picklist starts with surface-level heuristics: parameter size, licensing, and published perf on our profile. Then we apply workload heuristics: chat vs completion, typical prompt length, and memory usage patterns. These feed into an initial shortlist. Sometimes the name mapping is off in the transcript — e.g., "KV cash" instead of KV cache, sorry for that.

[03:12] Jonas Meyer: Are you doing kernel mapping per GPU type? We run mixed infra — A100s and some 80GB H100s in our private cloud.

[03:25] Ethan Brooks: Yes, kernel mapping per device is part of compatibility. We'll produce a matrix by architecture (A100/H100), sequence length buckets, and quantization profiles. For H100 we sometimes see better llmperf-like kernels but for some open models the fp16 path is unstable, so we have a quantized fallback.

[04:02] Sofia Alvarez: show us an example of how you pick two pareto models for routing.

[04:18] Maya Chen: Sure — here's a sample picklist on the Console. (link) We start with a baseline accuracy filter — e.g. instruction-following score 0.8+, then cost threshold, then throughput. In the UI you can toggle to emphasis latency or emphasis quality which re-ranks models.

[05:00] [screen share noise; slight overlap] Ethan Brooks: I'll run a mock bench now on a small prompt set — nothing sensitive — just to show end-to-end. Running bench on model "mistral-open-10b" and "vanguard-7b-q" as a quantized alternative.

[05:30] [05:30] Ethan Brooks: initializing bench, note these are hosted bench runners in us-east-1; when you run in your private cluster the numbers will shift but the methodology's identical.

[06:05] Laura Kim: do you support our SAML SSO and RBAC scoping for service accounts? We'll need audit log forwarding to our SIEM.

[06:20] Maya Chen: Yes, we support SAML (SAML 2.0), SSO, and RBAC roles — and audit logs can be pushed to your log collector or to an S3-compatible store. We also integrate with KMS/HSM for key management. We'll attach the security pack after the call.

[06:48] Ravi Patel: Security is huge. We are SOC2 in progress — will you need a vendor questionnaire?

[06:58] Priya Nair: We usually supply an enterprise security packet: SOC2 attestation, encryption at rest/in transit details, key rotation policies, and an example third-party pen test report. We'll slide that in the follow-up.

[07:25] [07:25] Ethan Brooks: Bench results first pass: mistral-open-10b: p50 48ms, p95 130ms, cost est 0.22 $/1k tokens; vanguard-7b-q: p50 62ms, p95 160ms, cost est 0.09 $/1k tokens. Notice kv-cache hit varies by instruction length — in chat scenarios caching reduces cost by ~18% on repeated prefixes.

[08:10] Jonas Meyer: Those numbers look good. How do you ensure reproducibility of the bench? We need deterministic seeds for a fair comparison.

[08:25] Ethan Brooks: We provide bench harnesses with fixed RNG seeds, fixed tokenization library versions, and container images. You can also bring your own container to run in private infra. The bench script we shared is the same harness.

[09:00] Maya Chen: Quick detour on routing: you can route by policy — latency SLO, cost cap, region. E.g. requests from EU can prefer region variants, and a canary model can sit behind a 5% rollout. If capacity dips we fallback to a compatible quantized variant.

[09:40] Laura Kim: On fallbacks — how does inference maintain coherent session KV across variant switch?

[09:52] Ethan Brooks: Good question. We keep a KV cache abstraction and for compatible variants we'll map keys; for incompatible models we do a short re-embedding and warm-up pass. There's a small latency bump when you change families but the Console surfaces a migration plan.

[10:35] Ravi Patel: Cost question: hosted vs dedicated — what's the break-even we should expect?

[10:45] Priya Nair: General rule: for sustained traffic > X rps (we'll provide concrete numbers) Dedicated becomes more cost effective; also Dedicated gives you pinned capacity and region control. Hosted is faster to iterate, cheaper for bursty workloads. We'll prepare a delta estimate for your expected load.

[11:30] [11:30] Ethan Brooks: Switching gears — here's a sample compatibility matrix we export. Rows: models and quant profiles; columns: GPU type, sequence bucket, kernel path and notes. For example, "mistral-open-10b" shows FP16 on H100 with optimized kernel, on A100 it falls back to slower path, and quantized variant runs on both.

[12:15] Sofia Alvarez: Is the compatibility matrix auto-generated after bench runs?

[12:25] Ethan Brooks: Yes, the Optimize pipeline analyzes profiling traces and produces the matrix; you can also push custom kernel metrics if you compile your own kernels.

[13:00] [13:00] Laura Kim: We have regulatory requirement to keep some logs in EU data centers only — can you confirm region tagging and retention controls?

[13:12] Maya Chen: We have region tagging and retention policies per customer. For Private deployments we give full control; for Hosted you can set region constraints and we can restrict replication. We'll include a short doc about retention SLAs.

[13:45] [13:45] Ethan Brooks: Also note that for on-prem we support the Private control plane model which gives you the ability to manage storage and logs locally. There's a small management fee for Private deployments.

[14:20] Ravi Patel: Any customers running mixed cloud + on-prem like we plan?

[14:30] Maya Chen: Yes, a few finserv and healthcare customers do hybrid routing — they keep PHI and PII on-prem, and use hosted for non-sensitive batch workloads. We can show an example architecture diagram post-call.

[15:00] [15:00] Ethan Brooks: Back to benching: we recommend a two-stage bench: shortlist 6-8 models using catalog heuristics, run a lightweight latency and quality test (24-48 hours), then pick 2-3 candidates for a longer, full-data bench. That lets you balance cost to get signal.

[15:42] Laura Kim: For quality signals do you run evals or human raters?

[15:50] Priya Nair: We run automated evals (instr-follow, LLM-judge style) and you can plug in human-in-the-loop tests through Redwood Console's eval integration. We'll show a sample eval set.

[16:30] Jonas Meyer: What about tokenization mismatches between model families? We saw issues when switching between bpe and sentencepiece.

[16:45] Ethan Brooks: We normalize tokenization in the bench harness and surface tokenization delta in the compat matrix — if you have a mixed fleet of models we'll flag tokenization drift.

[17:20] [17:20] Ravi Patel: Competitors — we ran a quick proof against MegaCloud AI endpoints earlier and saw similar latency but higher cost. What advantages are you offering on ops?

[17:35] Maya Chen: Ops-wise: unified runtime, transparent kernel mapping, prefix caching, and route policies are differentiators. We also operate the bench harness and give you the artifacts for audits.

[18:05] Sofia Alvarez: In the UI can we tag models and create a shortlists folder for a project?

[18:15] Priya Nair: Yes, Console allows project folders, tags, and shareable picklists with collaborators. You can also pin a model version for rollout.

[18:50] Ethan Brooks: Quick demo: I'm creating a picklist and toggling the latency emphasis slider — you can see the ranking change; I'll export a CSV and also show the compatibility matrix export. (some typing noises)

[19:30] [19:30] Ethan Brooks: Export link (mock): https://redwood.ai/exports/compatibility-export-ff-7692.csv

[20:00] Laura Kim: About bench PRNG seeds — will results differ by container base image?

[20:12] Ethan Brooks: Slightly; we lock runtime libs in the containers we provide. When you run on your infra, differences come from kernel versions and GPU microcode. We'll note that in the bench report.

[21:05] Ravi Patel: If we pick Dedicated, what's the SLA on latency and availability?

[21:15] Maya Chen: Dedicated comes with a 99.9% uptime SLA and latency SLO commitments per model family depending on configuration. We'll include a draft SLA in the follow-up.

[22:00] [22:00] Sofia Alvarez: Any pitfalls you've seen in migrations?

[22:12] Ethan Brooks: Biggest are tokenization drift, embedding dimensional mismatches for downstream rerank, and misconfigured KV cache warming. We recommend a staging test with shadow traffic to catch these.

[23:00] Priya Nair: Also note model licensing: some open weights have restrictive redistribution clauses; our catalog flags license compatibility.

[23:40] [23:40] Maya Chen: Ok we'll open the floor for questions.

[24:00] Laura Kim: Do you provide pre-built quantization recipes? We have teams that prefer 4-bit quant but worried about quality drop.

[24:20] Ethan Brooks: Yes, Optimize suggests quant profiles per workload and reports quality deltas. In some cases 4-bit with per-channel scales retains parity for instruction tasks; in other cases we suggest 8-bit. We'll include sample quantization deltas in the bench report.

[25:00] Jonas Meyer: Can I get the bench logs and perf traces to ingest into our observability stack?

[25:12] Ethan Brooks: Absolutely — we can export traces as OTLP or as raw pprof-like files. We'll provide a short how-to.

[26:00] Ravi Patel: Ok I want to make sure cost controls exist — per-route token caps, rate limits, and quotas.

[26:18] Priya Nair: Console supports per-route caps, token budgets, and spend alerts; you can lock a route to a model family to prevent accidental promotion.

[27:00] [27:00] Maya Chen: Quick recap: shortlist via heuristics -> run lightweight bench -> produce compat matrix -> pick finalists -> longer bench -> pilot deploy.

[27:30] Sofia Alvarez: On the pilot, what's the minimum time we need to see stable metrics?

[27:40] Ethan Brooks: For throughput/latency you can see signal in 48h; for quality/regression detection we recommend 2-3 weeks with sampled user traffic.

[28:05] [28:05] Laura Kim: Can Redwood handle encryption-in-use for our most sensitive workloads?

[28:20] Maya Chen: We support KMS integration and HSM-based key management; for deeper encryption-in-use we can discuss attested enclaves (EPC) in Private setups — that's more bespoke.

[29:00] Jonas Meyer: Any notes about kernel upgrades affecting inference? We had a case where a kernel patch changed perf by 12%.

[29:12] Ethan Brooks: We version kernel packs and have a compatibility tag; we also test regressions in our nightly bench. If a kernel upgrade is risky you can pin kernel version on Dedicated.

[30:00] [30:00] Ravi Patel: Great, I think I have enough. Can you send a tailored bench script and an estimated cost delta for 500 qps?

[30:12] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll send the bench script and a cost estimate. Ethan will outline the runbook.

[31:00] Ethan Brooks: I'll note the runbook: 1) run shortlist bench for 48h on 8 models; 2) analyze p95 and kv-cache hit; 3) export compat matrix; 4) pick 2 models for production pilot. I'll attach the bench harness link.

[31:45] Priya Nair: Also attaching sample picklist templates and the catalog heuristics doc.

[32:10] [32:10] Laura Kim: Any additional pricing for audit logs retention beyond default?

[32:22] Maya Chen: Yes, long-term retention and SSO integrations are part of enterprise add-ons; we'll include a pricing note.

[33:00] Sofia Alvarez: What about success criteria for pilot? We want to tie it to p95 < 200ms and cost < $0.15 per 1k tokens for baseline traffic.

[33:15] Priya Nair: Noted — we'll bake those as pilot SLAs.

[34:00] [34:00] Quick pause for small interruptions, background noise noted.

[34:25] Ethan Brooks: One more thing — if you have heavy embedding needs, we recommend separating embedding pipelines and using dedicated embedding models with batch-optimized paths; that lowers per-embedding unit price.

[35:05] Jonas Meyer: Ok thanks, that helps.

[35:30] Laura Kim: Could you also include a comparison table vs MegaCloud that lists key op features?

[35:45] Maya Chen: We'll produce a competitor matrix and share it.

[36:10] [36:10] Ethan Brooks: Running a short quality eval now on the two finalists: small sample of 200 prompts; automated judge score: mistral-open-10b 0.82, vanguard-7b-q 0.74. This informs the quality vs cost delta.

[36:45] Ravi Patel: Good to see numbers. Any known license issues for these weights?

[36:55] Priya Nair: We'll include license flags; vanguard-7b-q has a permissive license, mistral-open-10b has some redistribution caveats for commercial redistribution. We'll flag it.

[37:30] [37:30] Sofia Alvarez: Ok let's talk timeline: bench this week, kick pilot next monday?

[37:45] Maya Chen: We can aim for a week-of kickoff; prefer to have the bench results before pilot so we pick the right candidates.

[38:10] Jonas Meyer: Anything else on infra?

[38:20] Ethan Brooks: We'll need a short network whitelist for hosted bench runners to talk to your webhook for evals; we'll send IP ranges.

[38:52] Ravi Patel: I'll action providing dataset size and residency items.

[39:05] [39:05] Maya Chen: Final recap of next steps: send bench script + picklist templates + security pack + cost delta estimate + competitor matrix. Schedule pilot kickoff.

[39:30] Laura Kim: Sounds good. Thanks all.

[39:45] [39:45] Meeting ends with a brief chat about calendar invites and who to include.

End of transcript.
